Rocket Lab ($RKLB) won a $397 million U.S. Space Force SB-AMTI contract to develop, launch, and operate multiple sensor-equipped Flatellites.

The Details:

•	End-to-end scope: Rocket Lab will design, build, launch, and operate the satellites from secure facilities.

•	Neutron launches: The company plans to launch the Flatellites on its upcoming Neutron rocket.

•	Mission role: The satellites will provide tracking and data through secure, low-latency, high-bandwidth communications.

•	Expansion option: The contract includes an option for additional Flatellites within its total value.

Sunrun ($RUN) priced a $267 million public securitization backed by residential solar and storage leases and power purchase agreements.

The Details:

•	Structure: The deal includes Class A notes rated A- and Class B notes rated BB-, which Sunrun will retain.

•	Pricing: Class A notes carry a 6.28% coupon, a 200-bps spread, and a 6.33% yield.

•	Collateral: The portfolio covers 37,595 systems across 42 utility territories in 13 states.

A senior Middle East diplomat told MS NOW that U.S. and European pressure on Oman could lead to a temporary Iran-Oman agreement on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

The Details:

•	Route control: The diplomat said the deal could give Iran temporary control of both inward and outward shipping routes.

•	Waterway split: The inward route would run entirely through Iranian waters, while part of the outward route also crosses Iranian waters.

•	Oman talks: An Iranian official said Tehran is negotiating with Oman on a joint monitoring mechanism for the strait.

•	U.S. role: The Iranian official said the U.S. has not been allowed into the talks and will not be involved in regional decisions.

Bottom Line: The final terms are unclear, but the reported deal would expand Iran’s leverage over the strait.

*US NEARS HORMUZ DEAL, AIMING FOR WEDNESDAY ANNOUNCEMENT: AXIOS



*U.S., IRAN, OMAN NEAR 60-DAY INTERIM DEAL TO REOPEN STRAIT OF HORMUZ



*PROPOSED AGREEMENT SETS INBOUND TRAFFIC IN IRANIAN WATERS, OUTBOUND IN OMANI WATERS



*HORMUZ DEAL EXCLUDES TOLLS OR TRANSIT FEES DURING INITIAL 60-DAY PERIOD



*PARTIES AGREE TO CLEAR NAVAL MINES FROM HORMUZ MEDIAN LANE WITHIN 30 DAYS

U.S., Iran, and Oman are nearing a 60-day interim Strait of Hormuz arrangement, with Washington aiming to announce it Wednesday, according to Axios.

The Details:

•	Ship routes: Inbound vessels would use a northern lane through Iranian waters, while outbound ships would use a southern Omani lane coordinated with Iran.

•	Fees: No tolls or fees would apply during the 60-day temporary period.

•	Mine clearance: Parties would seek to clear naval mines from the median lane within 30 days.

•	Approval: Iranian leadership reportedly completed its approval process Tuesday.

Bottom Line: The proposed arrangement would temporarily reopen Hormuz while Iran and Oman negotiate a permanent traffic regime.

Samsung and SK Hynix test Chinese chip tools — Reuters



Samsung and SK Hynix are evaluating AMEC etching equipment at Chinese factories as a contingency against tighter U.S. controls on Western-tool imports and servicing.

The Details:

•	Testing: The Korean memory makers began evaluating AMEC equipment about two years ago, with no decision on broad deployment.

•	Factory exposure: Samsung’s Xi’an NAND plant and SK Hynix’s Dalian NAND and Wuxi DRAM plants rely heavily on Applied Materials and Lam Research tools.

•	Cost edge: Chinese chip tools can cost 20% to 30% less than comparable foreign equipment.

•	Policy backdrop: U.S. licenses cover maintaining existing China operations but not capacity expansion or technology upgrades.
